messages:
incidents-bot: PAGE: KV cache anomaly detected in us-west-2 cluster (auto-threshold). metric=continuous_batch_queue_depth, hostpool=kvcache-pool-4. latency P95 ↑ 3x, 5xx ↑ 1.8x. paging oncall @sre-rotation. alert: https://monitoring.internal/alerts/AC-9876 :rotating_light:

rajesh: oncall here, looking. grabbing logs and checking topology.

rajesh: quick summary so far — around 11:03 UTC we saw continuous batching queue depth spike, which correlated with a prefetch surge from a small subset of tenants that send large sequence requests. KV cache eviction rate jumped, followed by pack-shed events.

emily: seeing correlated increase in batch scheduler wait times — mixed short+long requests getting queued behind long requests. tail latency hits for short requests.

miguel: logs from kvcache primary: 
```
2026-03-15T11:03:22Z kvcache[pool=4] INFO prefetch: tenant=acme-corp req_id=xyz size=1.4MB
2026-03-15T11:03:23Z kvcache[pool=4] WARN eviction-rate=12.3x free_slots=4
2026-03-15T11:03:24Z batch-scheduler[slot=7] DEBUG pack: request=long-ctx tenant=acme-corp batching=continuous delay_ms=980
```

rajesh: initial mitigation plan — throttle prefetch for offending tenant group, reduce continuous batching window to favor latency SLOs, and temporarily enforce fairness by limiting long-request packing per-slot.

support-liz: customer impact — support signals increased 5xx and slow responses for several mid-market tenants (AcmeCorp, BlueHealth). They reported client timeouts around 10-12s. No data loss reported.

sre-rotation: executing tactical controls now. applying config patch to reduce continuous batching window from 200ms -> 60ms and set per-slot long-request limit=1.

sre-rotation: command I'm running:
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/configs/apply \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -d '{"service":"batch-scheduler","env":"prod","patch":{"continuous_batch_window_ms":60,"max_long_requests_per_slot":1}}'
```

miguel: rolling this to us-west-2 pool-4 now (canary 10% -> 50% -> all). watching eviction-rate and short-request P95.

rajesh: can someone drop the quick query for tenants with heavy long-requests? I want a list to throttle prefetch specifically.

emily: query: `select tenant, avg(request_len) from request_metrics where window=1m and region='us-west-2' order by avg desc limit 20` — returning acme-corp, bluehealth, studio-zen.

support-liz: I'm opening temp rate-limits for those tenants via support-controls to protect other customers. message drafted for customers: "We're applying temporary rate adaption to maintain latency SLA. No action required on your side."

product-ana: customer comms ok, keep me in loop for any escalations. prioritize BlueHealth — they're on dedicated SLAs.

incidents-bot: ACTION: runbook step 3 triggered — enable kv-prefetch-throttle for tenant list id=pf-2026-03-15-01. Link: https://infra/internal/runbooks/kv-prefetch-throttle

rajesh: throttle applied. patch id pf-2026-03-15-01. Observing drop in eviction-rate and queue depth within 90s. short-request P95 recovered ~70%.

miguel: after canary -> full roll, evictions back to baseline, pack-shed events stopped. still watching tail latency for a few slots.

emily: important note — the root appears to be aggressive prefetch combined with continuous batching heuristics that pack long contexts aggressively, starving short-paths when a small number of tenants send many large requests concurrently.

rajesh: next steps: 1) revert continuous batching window to 200ms config but add adaptive mode that reduces window when queue_depth > X and short_request_p95 > Y. 2) create scheduler fairness rule to prefer short requests when mixed queue ratio > 3:1. 3) postmortem and evals to reproduce workload.

support-liz: impacted customers notified (AcmeCorp, BlueHealth, Studio-Zen). tickets created: #INC-4321, #INC-4322, #INC-4323.

product-ana: tag these customers for potential credits if SLA breached.

rajesh: I'm going to open a follow-up ticket for an auto-throttle for prefetch that's tenant-aware (limit total prefetch per-tenant per-window).

miguel: open PR for scheduler change with tests, marking as high priority. devs: please review: https://git.internal/r/redwood/batch-scheduler/pulls/3291

emily: quick note for oncall handover — I'll be first responder for the next 2 hours, then @sre-rotation will hand over to next rotation. keep me CCed on any new alerts.

sre-rotation: thanks. adding timeline to incident log. ETA for follow-up patch (adaptive window + fairness) is EOD today if no blocking reviews.

rajesh: final status for now: mitigation applied (throttle + reduced window), customer impact contained, metrics recovering. moving to monitoring mode and will follow up with a postmortem doc.

emily: postmortem ticket created: PM-2026-03-15-kv-batch-hunger. assigning owners: raesh (root cause), miguel (scheduler fix), emily (postmortem), support-liz (customer follow-up).

support-liz: will send consolidated customer note in 2 hours.

product-ana: please add retrospective action for improved lab replay of mixed long/short workloads to CI.

rajesh: thanks team. I'll update this thread with any regressions or if the metrics stop improving. :thumbsup:
